answer:
Use OpenFOAM solver interFoam for a transient, two-phase sloshing simulation.
Model the rectangular tank with length 1.0 m in x, height 0.6 m in y, and width 0.1 m in z.
Create one 2D verification mesh with blockMesh using 200 by 120 by 1 cells and empty front/back boundaries.
Create one fully 3D mesh with blockMesh using 200 by 120 by 20 cells and wall boundaries on the front and back.
Set gravity to g = (0, -9.81, 0).
Set water density to 1000 kg/m3 and kinematic viscosity to 1e-6 m2/s.
Set air density to 1 kg/m3 and kinematic viscosity to 1.48e-5 m2/s.
Use laminar flow modeling.
Initialize U to (0, 0, 0) everywhere.
Initialize p_rgh to 0.
Initialize alpha.water using setFields with boxToCell slices so the free surface rises linearly from 0.25 m at x = 0 to 0.35 m at x = 1.0 m, with alpha.water = 1 below the local height and alpha.water = 0 above it.
Set the top patch as an atmospheric opening, with U using pressureInletOutletVelocity, p_rgh using totalPressure with p0 = 0, and alpha.water using inletOutlet with inletValue 0.
Set the bottom and side walls as no-slip walls, with U using fixedValue (0, 0, 0), p_rgh using zeroGradient, and alpha.water using zeroGradient.
Set the front and back patches to empty for the 2D case and to no-slip walls for the 3D case.
Set endTime to 10 seconds, deltaT to 1e-3, adjustTimeStep to yes, maxCo to 0.5, and writeInterval to 0.05 seconds.
Run the 2D case first to verify the setup, then run the 3D case.
Apply no external forcing after initialization; the sloshing is driven only by the tilted initial free surface under gravity.
